answer: Agents must anchor identity by reserving 1,000 slots of compute capacity at a registry, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent holds a jade token of reserved cycles to verify tenure. A verifier monitors the lagoon of incoming traffic for structural overlaps; honest agents pay for one slot while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture in the registry vault when an occupancy violation is detected. We assume issuers verify non-shared occupancy to ensure fakes incur prohibitive costs that dwarf any honest node investment.
